title: Coproduct Ext computed by one injective resolution, with natural degree-zero comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site in the chosen universe [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology, def-weil-size-convention], let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings and let $F$ and $(E_i)_{i\in I}$ be $R$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], where $I$ is a set. There exists a nonnegative injective resolution [def-sp-injective-resolutions] $0\to F\xrightarrow{\iota}J^0\xrightarrow{d_J^0}J^1\to\cdots$, extended by zero in negative degrees. For any such resolution and any $R$-module sheaf $M$, form the Hom cochain complex [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with $L_J(M)^q=\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,J^q)$ with differential $h\mapsto d_J^q\circ h$; the groups $\operatorname{Ext}_R^q(M,F):=H^qL_J(M)$ for $q\geq0$ are independent of the chosen injective resolution. For any small set $A$ and function $i:A\to I$, put $M=\bigoplus_{a\in A}E_{i(a)}$ and write $j_a:E_{i(a)}\to M$ for the coproduct inclusions. Restriction $h\mapsto(h\circ j_a)_a$ is an isomorphism of complexes $L_J(M)\cong\prod_{a\in A}L_J(E_{i(a)})$ and induces isomorphisms of abelian groups
$$H^qL_J(M)\cong\prod_{a\in A}H^qL_J(E_{i(a)})\qquad(q\geq0).$$
The map $\operatorname{Hom}_R(M,F)\to H^0L_J(M)$ sending $h$ to the class of $\iota\circ h$ is an isomorphism, natural for precomposition by every map between such coproducts. Consequently, if $\operatorname{Ext}_R^q(E_i,F)=0$ for all $i\in I$ and $q>0$, then $H^qL_J(M)=0$ for all $q>0$. These assertions also hold for any specified isomorphism $M'\cong M$ by precomposition, and include the empty coproduct and repeated summands.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaves-grothendieck], $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$ is Grothendieck abelian and has all small coproducts. By [lem-sp-grothendieck-enough-injectives] it has enough injectives. Part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] supplies the required resolution of $F$, zero in negative degrees. The site and module universe are the same chosen universe, so the coproduct indexed by the small set $A$ exists.

proof.text: Fix any such $J$. The differential squares to zero since $d_J^{q+1}d_J^q=0$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ext-via-injective-resolution] with $\mathcal A=\operatorname{Mod}(R)$, $N=F$, and arbitrary $M$. It identifies $H^qL_J(M)$ with the resolution-independent group $\operatorname{Ext}^q_{\mathcal A}(M,F)$ for every $q\geq0$, proving independence of the chosen resolution.

source.place: Tag 06XR (lemma-compute-ext-resolutions), part (1), specialized to objects in degree zero; sites-cohomology.tex Tag 07AA (example-hom-complex-into-sheaf).

proof.text: For each $q$, the coproduct universal property gives a unique $h:M\to J^q$ with $h j_a=h_a$ for every family $(h_a)_a$. Thus restriction $\rho^q(h)=(h j_a)_a$ is bijective and additive, with additive inverse given by this universal property. Associativity gives $(d_J^q h)j_a=d_J^q(hj_a)$, so $\rho$ and its inverse commute with the differentials. This proves the stated isomorphism of complexes.

source.place: Tag 07AC (lemma-existence-derived-lower-shriek), proof: direct sums of the modules under consideration; elementary coproduct universal property, expanded here.

proof.text: Put $K_a=L_J(E_{i(a)})$, $Z_a^q=\ker d_a^q$ and $B_a^q=\operatorname{im}d_a^{q-1}$. Apply [lem-pc-abelian-groups-exact-products] to $0\to Z_a^{q-1}\to K_a^{q-1}\to B_a^q\to0$ and $0\to B_a^q\to Z_a^q\to H^qK_a\to0$. The first gives $\operatorname{im}(\prod_a d_a^{q-1})=\prod_a B_a^q$; cycles are $\prod_a Z_a^q$ coordinatewise. The second identifies their quotient with $\prod_a H^qK_a$. The resulting map sends $[(z_a)_a]$ to $([z_a])_a$. Composing with $H^q(\rho)$ proves the required cohomology isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 07AC (lemma-existence-derived-lower-shriek), proof: Ext vanishing passes to direct sums; expansion using exact products in Ab, not exact products of sheaves.

proof.text: Exactness of $0\to F\xrightarrow{\iota}J^0\to J^1$ says that $\iota$ identifies $F$ with $\ker d_J^0$. Therefore each cycle $z:M\to J^0$ factors uniquely as $\iota h$. There are no degree-zero boundaries since $J^{-1}=0$. This proves that $h\mapsto[\iota h]$ is an additive isomorphism. For any $f:N\to M$, $(\iota h)f=\iota(hf)$, proving the asserted precomposition naturality, including maps that mix summands.

source.place: Tag 05TD (lemma-left-exact-higher-derived), proof, final paragraph: degree-zero kernel calculation, written directly for Hom.

proof.text: If each positive $\operatorname{Ext}^q_R(E_i,F)$ vanishes, step 2 makes every factor in step 4 zero, hence $H^qL_J(M)=0$. A specified isomorphism $u:M^{\prime}\to M$ induces the cochain isomorphism $h\mapsto hu$ with inverse $h\mapsto hu^{-1}$, preserving the degree-zero formula by step 5. Nothing requires distinct summands. For $A=\varnothing$, $M=0$, all Hom groups are zero and the empty product is the zero abelian group, so all assertions remain valid.

source.place: Tag 07AC (lemma-existence-derived-lower-shriek), proof: vanishing for direct sums; elementary consequences of preceding steps.
